implementation.approach: The Supabase client no longer consumes the callback URL itself (detectSessionInUrl:false), because doing so erased the type=invite flag that is the only signal distinguishing a user who must still choose a password. The callback is now parsed explicitly, the address bar is scrubbed before the token is spent, and the obligation to set a password is recorded so a reload mid-setup returns to it.
implementation.failure_precedence: ERROR is classified before TOKENS, so an expired invite can never be read as a session

unblock_steps: Open the official Supabase invite already sent to you and follow the link in a browser.
On the password-setup screen that opens, enter a password only you know, twice.
Sign out, then sign in at https://bibi-workspace-18.vercel.app with the email and that password.
Report success or failure only. Never send the password itself through any channel.

redirect_target_resolution.why_interactive_this_time: The earlier accidental change happened precisely because a push auto-confirmed in a non-TTY session. Running it interactively meant the full pending diff was displayed and consciously approved before anything was applied, which is what makes the next line meaningful.

diff_shown_before_applying.significance: The confirmation prompt renders the full config comparison, not a filtered view. Exactly two pending differences appeared, so every unrelated auth setting — TOTP enrol and verify, email confirmations, max_frequency, otp_length, and the signup setting closed under A24 — was already identical to the declared config and was left untouched. This is the direct contrast with the earlier non-TTY push that silently moved seven fields.
